## Family lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/family-lawyer/

A family lawyer represents you in the Family Courts for khula, divorce, child custody, maintenance and dowry recovery. Under the Family Courts Act 1964, these cases are filed in the family court of the area where the wife ordinarily resides. MeraLawyer.pk matches you with a family advocate in Islamabad or Rawalpindi and gives you the full fee before you start.

Cases handled:
- Khula: Dissolution of marriage at the wife's request through the Family Court.
- Divorce (talaq): Talaq notice to the Union Council and the 90-day reconciliation process.
- Child custody: Custody (hizanat) and guardianship petitions under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.
- Maintenance: Monthly maintenance for wife and children, including arrears.
- Dowry and gifts recovery: Recovery of dowry articles, gold and gifts after separation.
- Restitution of conjugal rights: Petitions to restore the marital home.
- Court marriage: Nikah before a nikah registrar with full documentation.
- Guardianship certificate: Legal guardianship of a minor for property, school or travel.

Key facts:
- Family cases in Islamabad and Rawalpindi are heard by the Family Courts under the Family Courts Act 1964.
- A khula, maintenance or dowry suit is usually filed where the wife ordinarily resides.
- Family courts are directed to decide cases within six months of the defendant's first appearance (section 12-A).
- Divorce and khula take effect through the Union Council or Arbitration Council after the 90-day period under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961.
- Child custody and guardianship are decided under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, with the welfare of the child as the main test.

### When should you hire a family lawyer in Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

You should speak to a family lawyer as soon as a marriage, custody or maintenance dispute becomes difficult to settle within the family. Early advice protects your position: a lawyer can tell you which court has jurisdiction, what evidence to preserve (nikah nama, receipts for dowry articles, bank transfers, messages) and whether a negotiated settlement is realistic before anything is filed.
Many people wait until they receive a court summons or a talaq notice. By then, deadlines are running and documents may be lost. A short consultation at the start usually costs far less than repairing a case later, and it gives you a clear picture of the time and fees involved in Islamabad or Rawalpindi.
- You want to file for khula or have received a khula notice
- Your spouse has sent or received a talaq notice through the Union Council
- You need maintenance for yourself or your children, including arrears
- You are seeking custody, visitation or a guardianship certificate
- You want dowry articles, gold or gifts returned after separation
- You plan a court marriage and want the paperwork done correctly

### How does a family case move through the Family Court?

A family suit starts with a plaint filed in the Family Court that has territorial jurisdiction. The court issues summons, the defendant files a written statement, and the judge holds a pre-trial hearing to attempt reconciliation. If reconciliation fails, the court frames issues, records evidence from both sides and then decides the case. In a khula suit, the court can pass a decree at the pre-trial stage if reconciliation fails.
After a decree, the work is not always finished. Maintenance decrees often need execution proceedings to recover money, and custody orders may need to be enforced. Your lawyer should explain these later stages at the start so you know the full path, not only the first hearing.

### Which family court will hear your case: Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

Jurisdiction mostly depends on where the wife ordinarily resides, or in custody matters, where the minor ordinarily lives. If the wife lives in an Islamabad sector such as G-9, I-8 or F-10, the case usually goes to the Family Courts in Islamabad. If she lives in Satellite Town, Saddar, Chaklala or Bahria Town Rawalpindi, the case usually goes to the Family Courts at the Rawalpindi district courts.
Filing in the wrong court causes delays and can lead to the plaint being returned. Because the twin cities sit side by side and many families move between them, checking jurisdiction carefully is one of the first things a family lawyer in Islamabad or Rawalpindi does.

### What documents should you bring to a family lawyer?

Bring whatever you have; your lawyer will tell you what else to collect. Copies are enough for the first meeting, but keep originals safe because the court may ask to see them.
- Nikah nama (marriage certificate) and NADRA marriage registration certificate, if issued
- CNICs of both spouses and B-forms or birth certificates of children
- Any talaq notice, khula notice or Union Council correspondence
- List and receipts of dowry articles, jewellery and gifts
- Evidence of income or expenses relevant to maintenance (salary slips, school fee receipts, medical bills)
- Messages, call records or letters relevant to the dispute

### How much does a family lawyer cost, and what affects the fee?

There is no fixed government rate for lawyers' fees in Pakistan. The fee depends on the type of case, whether it is contested, the number of hearings expected and whether execution or appeal is likely. An uncontested khula or a court marriage is simpler than a contested custody case with several witnesses.
At MeraLawyer.pk the fee for your matter is agreed before work starts, and court fees, process fees and certified-copy charges are shown separately at actual cost. Ask any lawyer you speak to for the same clarity: what the fee covers, which stages are included and what happens if the case takes longer than expected.

### Can overseas Pakistanis run a family case without travelling?

Yes, in most cases. You can appoint a lawyer and a local attorney through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate. The lawyer files and attends hearings, and you follow progress through WhatsApp updates and video calls. Some stages, such as recording your own evidence, may need your presence or special arrangements, and your lawyer will tell you in advance if that is the case.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps with family matters

We match you with a family advocate who regularly appears in the Family Courts of Islamabad or Rawalpindi, depending on where your case belongs. You get a clear explanation in Urdu or English, a written list of the documents needed, the agreed fee, and an update after each hearing. Your details are shared only with the lawyer handling your matter.

Q: How much does a family lawyer charge in Islamabad?
A: Fees depend on the type of case, whether it is contested and how many hearings are expected. A simple uncontested matter costs far less than a contested custody case. MeraLawyer.pk gives you the full fee for your case after a free first call.

Q: How long does a family case take?
A: Section 12-A of the Family Courts Act 1964 directs family courts to decide cases within six months of the defendant's first appearance. Contested custody and maintenance cases can take longer in practice.

Q: Can I file a family case if I live abroad?
A: Yes. You can appoint a lawyer through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate, and follow the case by WhatsApp and video call.

Q: Which court hears a khula case?
A: The Family Court where the wife ordinarily resides, for example the family courts in Islamabad or Rawalpindi.

## Criminal lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/criminal-lawyer/

A criminal lawyer protects you from the moment an FIR is registered: applying for pre-arrest or post-arrest bail, challenging a false FIR, and defending you at trial. Bail is sought under sections 497 and 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Sessions Court or the High Court. Tell us your matter is urgent and we prioritise it.

Cases handled:
- Pre-arrest bail: Protective bail before arrest under section 498 CrPC.
- Post-arrest bail: Bail after arrest under section 497 CrPC.
- FIR registration: Help getting an FIR registered, including through a section 22-A petition.
- FIR quashment: Petitions to quash a false or malicious FIR.
- Trial defence: Defence before magistrates and sessions courts.
- Cyber crime: FIA cases under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016.
- Cheque dishonour: Cases under section 489-F of the Pakistan Penal Code.
- Appeals: Criminal appeals and revisions before the High Court.

Key facts:
- Bail in non-bailable offences is sought under section 497 (post-arrest) and section 498 (pre-arrest) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1898.
- A bail application is normally filed first in the Court of Session, and then in the High Court if refused.
- A false or malicious FIR can be challenged, including through quashment proceedings before the High Court.
- Cyber crime offences under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016 are investigated by the federal cyber crime agency and tried by designated courts.
- In Rawalpindi, criminal appeals and bail matters beyond the sessions court go to the Lahore High Court, Rawalpindi Bench; in Islamabad, to the Islamabad High Court.

### What should you do in the first hours after an FIR is registered?

The first hours matter most. Get a copy of the FIR and note the police station, the sections applied and the names of the complainant and investigating officer. Do not give statements or sign documents without legal advice. If the offence is non-bailable and you have not been arrested, a criminal lawyer can assess whether to apply for pre-arrest bail without delay.
If a family member has already been arrested, the lawyer can check whether the arrest and remand were lawful, apply for post-arrest bail, and make sure the person is produced before a magistrate within the time the law requires. Tell your lawyer at once if the matter is urgent so that it is prioritised.
- Collect the FIR number, police station and sections of law
- Do not contact the complainant or witnesses about the case
- Keep documents, messages and receipts that support your side
- Share any medical reports or evidence of an earlier dispute
- Call a lawyer before appearing at the police station

### What is the difference between pre-arrest and post-arrest bail?

Pre-arrest bail (also called protective or anticipatory bail) under section 498 CrPC protects a person from arrest. Courts grant it when the accused shows that the case appears to be motivated by mala fide intentions or ulterior motives, along with the usual grounds for bail. Post-arrest bail under section 497 CrPC is for a person already in custody, and the court considers the nature of the offence, the evidence and whether the case calls for further inquiry.
Offences that are bailable under the Code are different: the accused has a right to bail under section 496. A criminal lawyer reviews the sections in your FIR to tell you which route applies and how strong the grounds are.

### Which courts hear criminal matters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi?

In Islamabad, criminal trials and bail applications start in the District and Sessions Courts (East and West), with further remedies in the Islamabad High Court. In Rawalpindi, they start at the district courts at Kachehri, with further remedies in the Lahore High Court, Rawalpindi Bench. Special courts hear particular categories, such as anti-corruption, banking and cyber crime cases, and anti-terrorism matters are heard by anti-terrorism courts.
Choosing a lawyer who appears regularly in the relevant court is practical as well as legal: they know the procedure, the listing system and how to move an urgent application on the same day.

### How can a false FIR be challenged?

Several remedies exist, and the right one depends on the facts. The accused can join the investigation and produce evidence of innocence, ask senior police officers to change the investigation, seek bail, or apply to the High Court to quash the FIR or proceedings where the case is clearly an abuse of process. The complainant in a false case can also face legal consequences under the Pakistan Penal Code.
A careful lawyer will not promise quashment. They will explain which remedy has the best chance on your facts and what evidence will help, such as call records, CCTV footage, documents showing you were elsewhere, or proof of a prior civil dispute.

### What criminal cases do lawyers in the twin cities commonly handle?

Criminal lawyers in Islamabad and Rawalpindi handle a wide range of matters. Some of the most common are listed below; if your matter is not listed, describe it and we will match you with the right advocate.
- Cheque dishonour cases under section 489-F PPC
- Fraud, cheating and breach of trust
- Harassment, threats and defamation complaints
- Cyber crime complaints and defence under PECA 2016
- Narcotics cases under the Control of Narcotic Substances Act 1997
- Assault, hurt and property damage cases
- Criminal appeals and revisions

### How much does a criminal lawyer charge?

Fees depend on the court, the seriousness of the offence, the urgency and the stage of the case. A single bail application in the sessions court is priced differently from a full trial defence or a High Court petition. MeraLawyer.pk agrees the fee with you before the lawyer starts, so you know what each stage will cost.

### How MeraLawyer.pk handles urgent criminal matters

When you mark a matter as urgent, a case manager calls you back as a priority and connects you with a criminal advocate who can act quickly in the right court in Islamabad or Rawalpindi. You receive clear advice on what to do and what to avoid, and updates after each hearing by phone or WhatsApp.

Q: What is the difference between pre-arrest and post-arrest bail?
A: Pre-arrest bail (section 498 CrPC) protects you from arrest before it happens and is granted only in limited circumstances, such as a malicious case. Post-arrest bail (section 497 CrPC) is sought after you have been arrested.

Q: Can I get bail on the same day?
A: A bail petition can often be filed the same day, but the court decides when to hear it. In urgent matters an interim pre-arrest bail may be granted at the first hearing.

Q: What should I do if a false FIR is registered against me?
A: Do not ignore it. Speak to a criminal lawyer immediately about pre-arrest bail and whether the FIR can be challenged through a quashment petition.

Q: Do you handle FIA cyber crime cases?
A: Yes. Our criminal lawyers handle complaints and defence in FIA cyber crime cases under PECA 2016.

## Property lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/property-lawyer/

A property lawyer checks title before you buy, handles transfer and mutation, and takes disputes such as illegal possession, inheritance and rent cases to the civil courts. In Rawalpindi, land records are kept by the Punjab Land Records Authority; in Islamabad, by the ICT revenue office or the CDA, depending on the area. We verify the record before you pay.

Cases handled:
- Property verification: Title, fard and record checks before you buy.
- Transfer and registry: Sale deed, registry and mutation (intiqal).
- Illegal possession: Recovery under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005.
- Inheritance and partition: Dividing inherited property between legal heirs.
- Rent cases: Eviction and rent recovery before the rent controller.
- Stay orders: Injunctions to stop sale, construction or dispossession.
- Specific performance: Enforcing a sale agreement when the other side backs out.
- Recovery suits: Recovery of money under Order XXXVII CPC.

Key facts:
- Sale of immovable property worth one hundred rupees or more must be made by a registered instrument under the Transfer of Property Act 1882 and the Registration Act 1908.
- In Rawalpindi, land records are maintained digitally by the Punjab Land Records Authority through its service centres.
- In Islamabad, transfers in CDA sectors go through the Capital Development Authority, and in private societies through the society's transfer office.
- Federal advance taxes apply on purchase and sale of property, and provincial or ICT stamp duty applies on the transfer deed; rates change in annual Finance Acts.
- Verifying title, mutation history and approval status of the housing scheme before paying is the most effective way to avoid fraud.

### Why do you need a property lawyer before buying in Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

Property fraud usually happens before the sale, not after it. Fake files, double sales, forged powers of attorney and plots in unapproved housing schemes all look genuine until someone checks the records. A property lawyer checks title, compares documents with official records, and makes sure the payment schedule protects you until the transfer is complete.
The twin cities have several different systems. CDA sectors, private societies such as DHA and Bahria Town, cooperative societies, Rawalpindi Cantonment and Chaklala Cantonment areas, and rural land under PLRA all follow different procedures. A lawyer who works in Islamabad and Rawalpindi knows which office to approach for each one.

### What does a property lawyer check during due diligence?

Due diligence means confirming that the seller owns the property, has the right to sell it, and that nothing will stop the transfer. The exact checks depend on whether the property is in a CDA sector, a private society or a revenue estate.
- Title documents: registered sale deed, allotment letter, transfer letter or fard
- Mutation (intiqal) history and the current record of rights
- Approval status of the housing scheme with CDA or RDA
- Society NOC, dues clearance and any restriction on transfer
- Pending litigation, stay orders, mortgages or bank charges
- Identity of the seller and validity of any power of attorney
- Physical inspection to match the plot number, boundaries and possession

### How does a property transfer work in Islamabad and Rawalpindi?

A typical transfer has five stages: verification, agreement to sell with a token payment, payment of taxes, execution and registration of the sale deed (or society transfer), and mutation in the official record. In Islamabad CDA sectors, the transfer is processed by CDA. In private societies, the society's transfer office handles the change of ownership. For land recorded with the revenue department, the sale deed is registered before the Sub-Registrar and the mutation is entered in the land record.
Taxes are paid before registration: advance tax on the seller and buyer under the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, and stamp duty and other charges under ICT or Punjab law. Filers usually pay lower withholding rates than non-filers, so it helps to check your status on the Active Taxpayers List first.

### What property disputes do lawyers handle?

Not every property matter is a purchase. Property lawyers in Islamabad and Rawalpindi also act in disputes, many of which go before the civil courts or tribunals.
- Suits for specific performance of an agreement to sell
- Possession and illegal dispossession cases
- Partition of inherited property between heirs
- Rent and eviction cases before the Rent Controller or tribunal
- Cancellation of forged documents and fraudulent mutations
- Disputes with housing societies over allotment or transfer

### How do inheritance and property transfer work together?

When a property owner dies, the property passes to the legal heirs under their personal law. Heirs normally need a succession certificate or letters of administration for movable assets, and an inheritance mutation or society transfer for immovable property. A property lawyer coordinates both, so the property can later be sold or divided without objections.

### How much does a property lawyer charge?

Verification and transfer work is often priced per transaction, while disputes are priced by stage. Government taxes and fees are separate from the lawyer's fee. MeraLawyer.pk agrees the fee before work starts and gives you a written list of expected government charges so there are no surprises on the day of registration.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps with property matters

We match you with a property advocate who works with the relevant authority for your property, whether that is CDA, a private society, RDA or the PLRA service centres. You receive a verification report before you pay, help with the agreement and taxes, and support through registration and mutation. Overseas Pakistanis can complete most steps through a power of attorney.

Q: How do I verify a property before buying in Rawalpindi or Islamabad?
A: Ask for the fard (record of rights) or society allotment and transfer documents, then have a lawyer verify them with the land record office or housing society, check for pending litigation, and confirm the seller's identity.

Q: What can I do if someone illegally occupies my property?
A: You can file a complaint under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 and, in parallel, a civil suit for possession. Act quickly and keep proof of ownership.

Q: How is inherited property divided?
A: Shares are fixed by Islamic inheritance law for Muslims. Legal heirs can agree a family settlement, or any heir can file a partition suit in the civil court.

## Corporate and tax lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/corporate-lawyer/

A corporate lawyer sets up your business correctly and keeps it compliant: SECP company registration, NTN and sales tax registration with the FBR, annual tax returns, trademark registration with IPO Pakistan, and the contracts your business runs on. MeraLawyer.pk handles the filing for you and quotes a fixed fee upfront.

Cases handled:
- Company registration: Private limited, single-member and public companies with SECP.
- Income tax returns: Annual returns and wealth statements on FBR IRIS.
- NTN registration: National Tax Number for individuals, firms and companies.
- Sales tax registration: FBR for goods; FBR (ICT) or PRA for services.
- Trademark registration: Brand protection with IPO Pakistan.
- Contracts: Shareholder, partnership, employment and service agreements.
- Tax notices: Replies to FBR notices and appeals.
- Banking matters: Recovery suits and defence in banking courts.

Key facts:
- Companies in Pakistan are incorporated with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) under the Companies Act 2017.
- A single member company or private limited company can be registered online through SECP's e-services.
- Businesses register for income tax with FBR; sales tax on goods is with FBR, while sales tax on services is with FBR for Islamabad and the Punjab Revenue Authority for Rawalpindi.
- Trademarks are registered with the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan under the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001.
- Registered companies must file annual returns and keep statutory records; missed filings can lead to penalties.

### What does a corporate lawyer do for a business in Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

A corporate lawyer helps you set up the right business structure, register it, and keep it compliant. For a new business that usually means choosing between a sole proprietorship, a partnership, a single member company or a private limited company, registering with SECP and FBR, and putting basic contracts in place. For an existing business it means annual filings, shareholder changes, contracts, employment documents and disputes.
Good corporate advice is preventive. Clear shareholder agreements, properly drafted contracts and timely filings avoid most of the disputes and penalties that small businesses in the twin cities run into.

### Which business structure should you choose?

The right structure depends on liability, the number of owners, the need to raise investment and how clients or banks view the business. Your lawyer will explain the trade-offs, but the main options are summarised below.
- Sole proprietorship: simplest to start, registered for tax with FBR; the owner is personally liable
- Partnership: two or more partners; can be registered with the Registrar of Firms; partners share liability
- Single member company (SMC): one owner with limited liability, registered with SECP
- Private limited company: two or more members with limited liability; preferred for investment and contracts
- Limited liability partnership (LLP): registered with SECP; combines partnership flexibility with limited liability

### How is a company registered with SECP?

Registration starts with reserving a company name on SECP's online system, followed by filing the incorporation documents, including the memorandum and articles of association and the details of directors and subscribers. Once SECP approves the application, it issues a certificate of incorporation. Through integration between SECP and FBR, the company also receives its National Tax Number.
After incorporation, the company should open a bank account, register for sales tax if required, and set up its statutory registers. Your lawyer can also register the company with the relevant chamber of commerce in Islamabad or Rawalpindi if you need membership for trade or tenders.

### What ongoing compliance does a company need?

Incorporation is the start, not the end. Companies that miss filings face penalties and can find it hard to open accounts, bid for tenders or attract investors.
- Annual return filing with SECP and holding the annual general meeting where required
- Filing changes of directors, shareholding or registered office with SECP
- Annual income tax returns and monthly or quarterly withholding statements with FBR
- Monthly sales tax returns if registered with FBR or PRA
- Maintaining statutory registers and minutes of meetings

### Which contracts should every business have?

Most business disputes come from verbal deals or copied templates. A corporate lawyer drafts contracts that reflect Pakistani law and your actual arrangement, including payment terms, termination, dispute resolution and confidentiality.
- Shareholder or partnership agreement
- Service and supply agreements with clients and vendors
- Employment contracts and non-disclosure agreements
- Commercial rent agreement for your office or shop
- Software, franchise or distribution agreements where relevant

### Can foreign or overseas investors register a company in Pakistan?

Yes. Foreign nationals and overseas Pakistanis can be directors and shareholders of a Pakistani company. Some additional documents and security clearance may be required for foreign directors, and certain sectors have special rules. A corporate lawyer handles the process remotely, with documents attested where needed.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps businesses

We offer fixed-fee packages for SECP registration, NTN and sales tax registration, trademark filing and annual compliance, and connect you with a corporate advocate for contracts and disputes. Whether your business is in Blue Area, the I-9 or I-10 industrial areas, Saddar or on Murree Road, you can keep your legal work in one place, with fees agreed upfront.

Q: Do I need a lawyer to register a company?
A: It is not legally required, but a lawyer or corporate consultant ensures your memorandum and articles of association, shareholding and filings are correct, which prevents problems with banks, FBR and investors later.

Q: Is a sole proprietorship or a private limited company better?
A: A sole proprietorship is cheaper and faster to set up but you are personally liable for its debts. A private limited company separates your personal assets from the business and is preferred by banks, investors and large clients.

Q: When is the income tax return due in Pakistan?
A: For individuals and AOPs the due date is usually 30 September each year for the previous tax year, unless the FBR announces an extension.

## Lawyer for overseas Pakistanis
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/overseas-pakistani-lawyer/

Overseas Pakistanis can run legal matters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi without flying home. You appoint a lawyer through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate, then follow your case by WhatsApp and video call. We handle property recovery, family cases, succession, tax filing and document attestation.

Cases handled:
- Power of attorney: Drafting and guidance on embassy attestation.
- Property recovery: Removing illegal occupants from your property.
- Property management: Rent collection and tenant issues.
- Family cases from abroad: Khula, divorce and custody cases.
- Succession: Succession certificates and inheritance.
- Document attestation: MOFA, HEC, IBCC and embassy attestation.
- Overseas tax return: Non-resident tax filing with FBR.
- Police character certificate: For visa and employment abroad.

Key facts:
- Overseas Pakistanis can authorise a lawyer or relative in Pakistan through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate.
- A power of attorney executed abroad usually needs stamp duty paid in Pakistan before it is used.
- Most property, family and inheritance matters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi can be handled without travelling to Pakistan.
- Before paying for property in Pakistan, overseas buyers should have the title and the housing scheme's approval verified independently.
- Updates can be given by WhatsApp, email and video calls in Urdu or English.

### What legal problems do overseas Pakistanis most often face?

Distance creates risk. Property bought years ago may have been occupied, sold on the basis of a forged power of attorney, or caught in a family dispute. Inheritance can stall because heirs live in different countries. Family cases can be filed in Pakistan while one spouse lives abroad. An overseas Pakistani lawyer protects your interests in Islamabad and Rawalpindi while you live elsewhere.
- Illegal occupation of a house or plot
- Fraudulent sale or transfer using forged documents
- Inheritance disputes and succession certificates
- Divorce, khula, custody and maintenance cases filed in Pakistan
- Buying property safely from abroad
- Rent collection and tenant disputes

### How do you appoint a lawyer from abroad?

The usual route is a power of attorney. You sign it before the Pakistani embassy or consulate in your country of residence (or get a local notarisation followed by the required attestations). The original is sent to Pakistan, stamp duty is paid, and your lawyer or chosen attorney can then act for you before courts and authorities. A special power of attorney limited to a specific task is safer than a broad general power.
Before you sign, have your lawyer draft or review the wording. A badly drafted power of attorney is one of the most common causes of property fraud against overseas Pakistanis.

### How can you protect your property in Islamabad or Rawalpindi from abroad?

Simple steps reduce risk considerably. Keep certified copies of your title documents outside Pakistan, check the record periodically through the relevant authority, avoid giving general powers of attorney, and make sure tenants have written, registered agreements. In Islamabad and Rawalpindi, tenants should also be registered with the police under the applicable law.
If your property has been occupied or sold without your consent, act quickly. Your lawyer can file a complaint, seek an injunction to stop further transfers, and start civil or criminal proceedings as appropriate. Overseas Pakistanis in Punjab can also approach the Overseas Pakistanis Commission for facilitation.

### Can a family case in Pakistan be handled while you live abroad?

Yes. A lawyer can file or defend khula, divorce, maintenance and custody cases through a power of attorney, and many hearings proceed without your personal presence. For evidence, the court may require you to appear in person, record evidence through a commission, or use other arrangements. Your lawyer will plan this early, so you can book travel only when it is truly necessary.

### How does inheritance work when heirs live in different countries?

Each heir can authorise a lawyer or a relative in Pakistan through a power of attorney. The lawyer then applies for a succession certificate or letters of administration, completes inheritance mutation or society transfer, and, if the heirs agree, arranges sale and distribution. When heirs disagree, partition proceedings may be needed. Clear communication with all heirs from the start avoids most delays.

### How will you receive updates and documents?

We agree a communication plan at the start: updates by WhatsApp after each hearing, scanned copies of orders and documents by email, and video calls when decisions are needed. Consultations are available in Urdu or English and are scheduled to suit your time zone in the UK, Europe, the Gulf or North America.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps overseas Pakistanis

We match you with an advocate in Islamabad or Rawalpindi who regularly handles overseas clients, prepare the power of attorney wording, guide you through attestation, and manage the case locally with fees agreed before work starts.

Q: Can I fight a property case in Pakistan while living abroad?
A: Yes. You authorise a lawyer or a trusted relative through a power of attorney attested at the Pakistani embassy or consulate, and your lawyer appears in court for you.

Q: How do I attest a power of attorney abroad?
A: Sign it before the consular officer at the Pakistani embassy or consulate, or through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' online e-attestation and consular facilities where available. In Pakistan it may then need to be registered with the sub-registrar for property use.

Q: How will I know what is happening in my case?
A: Your lawyer sends an update after every hearing by WhatsApp, along with copies of orders when they are issued.

## Company registration in Pakistan with SECP
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/company-registration/

Company registration in Pakistan is done online with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). You reserve a company name, submit the memorandum and articles of association with director and shareholder details, pay the SECP fee, and receive a certificate of incorporation. We prepare and file everything for you.

Process:
1. Choose the structure: We advise on the company type, shareholding and number of directors.
2. Reserve the name: We search and reserve an available name with SECP.
3. Prepare documents: We draft the MOA and AOA and collect director details.
4. File with SECP: We submit the incorporation application and pay the fee.
5. Receive certificate: SECP issues your certificate of incorporation.
6. Register for tax: We register the company's NTN with the FBR.

Documents required:
- CNIC copies of all directors and shareholders (passport for foreigners)
- Proposed company names (three options)
- Registered office address and proof
- Nature of business
- Email and mobile number of each director
- Shareholding percentages

Laws: Companies Act 2017; Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2017

Key facts:
- Companies are registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) under the Companies Act 2017.
- The process is online: name reservation, filing incorporation documents, and issue of the certificate of incorporation.
- Through SECP and FBR integration, a newly incorporated company receives its National Tax Number.
- A single member company needs one member and a nominee; a private limited company needs at least two members.
- Foreign nationals and overseas Pakistanis can be directors and shareholders, subject to additional documents.

### Which type of company should you register?

Most small and medium businesses in Islamabad and Rawalpindi choose either a single member company or a private limited company. Both give limited liability, which protects your personal assets from business debts. The choice depends on how many owners there are and how you plan to grow.
- Single member company (SMC): one owner, one nominee director; good for freelancers, consultants and solo founders
- Private limited company: two or more members; best for partners, investors and companies bidding for contracts
- Limited liability partnership (LLP): suits professional firms that want partnership flexibility with limited liability
- Public or non-profit (section 42) companies: have extra requirements; ask us before choosing these

### How does SECP company registration work step by step?

First, choose two or three possible names and check that they are not identical or too similar to existing companies or trademarks. The name is reserved on SECP's online system. Next, the incorporation application is filed with the memorandum and articles of association, details of directors and subscribers, their CNICs or passports, and the registered office address. SECP examines the application and, if it is complete, issues the certificate of incorporation.
After incorporation, the company receives its NTN through the SECP and FBR integration. The next steps are opening a corporate bank account, registering for sales tax if your business requires it, and setting up the statutory registers that every company must keep.

### What documents do you need to register a company?

Registration is mostly online, so scanned copies are usually sufficient.
- CNIC (or passport for foreigners) of every director and shareholder
- Proposed company names and a short description of business activities
- Registered office address in Islamabad, Rawalpindi or elsewhere, with proof
- Email address and mobile number of each director
- Shareholding structure and paid-up capital
- For a single member company: CNIC and consent of the nominee

### Should the registered office be in Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

Both cities work well. The registered office determines which SECP company registration office oversees the company and where official notices are sent. Many businesses register in Islamabad, close to SECP's head office in Blue Area and the federal tax offices, while others register in Rawalpindi where their shop or office is located. For sales tax on services, the location of the business matters: services from Islamabad fall under FBR's Islamabad services law, and services from Rawalpindi under the Punjab Revenue Authority.

### What compliance does a company need after registration?

Every registered company must keep its records and filings up to date. Missing annual returns or changes leads to penalties and can block bank accounts or tender bids. Typical obligations are the annual return with SECP, notifying changes of directors, shareholders or address, filing annual income tax returns with FBR, monthly withholding statements, and monthly sales tax returns if registered.

### How long does company registration take?

Name reservation and incorporation are usually completed within a few working days if the documents are correct and the name is available. Delays happen when names are rejected, documents are incomplete or a foreign director needs security clearance. We check these points before filing to avoid rejections.

### How MeraLawyer.pk registers your company

We advise on the right structure, check name availability, prepare the memorandum and articles, file with SECP, and hand over the incorporation certificate and NTN. We can also register you for sales tax, file a trademark for your brand name, and handle annual compliance. The fee is agreed before work starts, and SECP fees are charged at actual cost.

Q: How long does company registration take in Pakistan?
A: When documents are complete, SECP often processes online incorporation within a few working days. Name objections or missing documents add time.

Q: What is the minimum number of directors?
A: A single-member company needs one director and one nominee. A private limited company needs at least two members and two directors.

Q: Can a foreigner register a company in Pakistan?
A: Yes. Foreign nationals can be shareholders and directors, subject to security clearance by the Ministry of Interior, which SECP arranges.

Q: Is there a minimum paid-up capital?
A: There is no general minimum for private companies, although some regulated sectors set their own requirements.

## Income tax return filing in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/income-tax-return/

An income tax return is filed online on the FBR's IRIS portal, usually by 30 September for the previous tax year. Individuals also file a wealth statement listing assets and liabilities. Filing puts you on the Active Taxpayers List, which lowers withholding tax on property, vehicles and banking. We prepare and file your return for you.

Process:
1. Share your details: Send salary certificates, bank statements and asset details.
2. We calculate tax: We work out your tax liability and adjustable taxes.
3. You review: You approve the return and wealth statement before filing.
4. We file on IRIS: We submit the return and send you the acknowledgement.

Documents required:
- CNIC
- IRIS login or registered mobile and email
- Salary certificate or business income records
- Bank account statements and withholding tax certificates
- Property, vehicle and investment details
- Previous year's return, if filed

Laws: Income Tax Ordinance 2001; Income Tax Rules 2002

Key facts:
- Income tax returns are filed with the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) through its IRIS portal under the Income Tax Ordinance 2001.
- Individuals usually also file a wealth statement under section 116, listing assets, liabilities and expenses.
- The deadline for individuals is usually 30 September for the tax year ending 30 June; FBR sometimes extends it.
- Filing on time places you on the Active Taxpayers List, which lowers withholding tax on property, vehicles and banking.
- Late filing can lead to penalties and removal from the Active Taxpayers List until you file.

### Who must file an income tax return in Pakistan?

You must file if your taxable income exceeds the minimum taxable threshold, and in several other situations set out in the Income Tax Ordinance, for example if you own certain property or a vehicle above a specified engine size, or hold an industrial or commercial electricity connection with high bills. Even when filing is not mandatory, many people file voluntarily to join the Active Taxpayers List and pay lower withholding taxes.
- Salaried individuals whose income exceeds the threshold
- Business owners, shopkeepers and freelancers
- Landlords earning rental income
- People buying or selling property or vehicles who want filer rates
- Company directors and members of associations of persons
- Overseas Pakistanis with income or assets in Pakistan

### What is the Active Taxpayers List and why does it matter?

The Active Taxpayers List (ATL) is FBR's list of people who have filed their return for the latest tax year. Being on the ATL means you pay lower withholding tax on many transactions, including property purchase and sale, vehicle registration, some bank transactions and dividends. The difference between filer and non-filer rates is often much larger than the cost of filing, which is why many people in Islamabad and Rawalpindi file even when their taxable income is low.

### How is an income tax return filed with FBR?

Filing happens online on IRIS. The return reports your income from salary, business, property, capital gains and other sources, the tax already deducted at source, and any tax payable or refundable. Individuals also file a wealth statement showing assets and liabilities at the year end, and a reconciliation showing how wealth changed during the year.
The wealth reconciliation is where most problems arise. Unexplained increases in wealth can trigger notices, so it is important to declare inheritances, gifts and loans properly. A tax lawyer or consultant prepares the return and wealth statement together so they match.

### What documents are needed to file a tax return?

Gather these for the tax year you are filing.
- CNIC and IRIS login, or details to register on IRIS
- Salary certificate and tax deduction certificate from the employer
- Bank statements and withholding tax certificates from banks
- Rental agreements and rent received, if any
- Property and vehicle documents, including purchase and sale details
- Utility bills, school fees and other major expenses
- Business records, invoices and expenses for business income

### What happens if you file late or receive an FBR notice?

Late filing can attract a penalty and keeps you off the Active Taxpayers List until you file, which means higher withholding taxes in the meantime. FBR may also issue notices asking you to file, explain your wealth, or respond to an audit. Do not ignore notices; reply within the time given or ask for more time. A lawyer can respond on your behalf and represent you before the Commissioner Inland Revenue at the Regional Tax Office in Islamabad or Rawalpindi.

### Can overseas Pakistanis and freelancers file returns?

Yes. Overseas Pakistanis with income or assets in Pakistan often file to keep filer status for property transactions. Freelancers earning through foreign remittances have special considerations, including the treatment of export of IT services. We prepare returns remotely and confirm the right treatment for your income.

### How MeraLawyer.pk files your return

Send us your documents by WhatsApp or email. We register you on IRIS if needed, prepare the return and wealth statement, review them with you, and file before the deadline. You receive copies of the filed return and acknowledgement. The fee is agreed upfront.

Q: What is the deadline for filing income tax returns?
A: The due date for individuals is normally 30 September for the tax year ending 30 June. The FBR sometimes extends it, so check the current year's announcement.

Q: What happens if I file late?
A: You can still file, but late filing can attract penalties and you may need to pay a surcharge to get onto the Active Taxpayers List for that year.

Q: Do overseas Pakistanis need to file returns?
A: Non-residents with Pakistan-source income, or who want lower withholding tax on property deals, often benefit from filing.

Q: What is a wealth statement?
A: A statement of your assets and liabilities at the end of the tax year, required with the return for most individuals.

## NTN registration in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/ntn-registration/

An NTN (National Tax Number) is your registration with the Federal Board of Revenue. For individuals, the NTN is the same as the CNIC number once registered on the FBR's IRIS portal. Businesses, AOPs and companies receive their own NTN. Registration needs a CNIC, a mobile number registered in your own name, an email and an address.

Process:
1. Send your details: CNIC, mobile, email, address and business information.
2. We register on IRIS: We complete the registration and verification codes.
3. Business details: We add business name, address and activity where needed.
4. Get your certificate: You receive your NTN certificate.

Documents required:
- CNIC
- Mobile number registered in your name
- Email address
- Residential and business address
- For AOPs: partnership deed and partners' CNICs
- For companies: certificate of incorporation

Laws: Income Tax Ordinance 2001, section 181

Key facts:
- NTN (National Tax Number) registration is done online with the Federal Board of Revenue through the IRIS portal.
- For individuals, the CNIC number is used as the NTN once registered on IRIS.
- Companies receive an NTN on incorporation through SECP and FBR integration; partnerships and AOPs register separately.
- Registration needs a mobile number and email registered in the applicant's own name.
- Having an NTN is the first step to filing returns and joining the Active Taxpayers List.

### Who needs an NTN in Pakistan?

Anyone who earns taxable income, runs a business, wants to file an income tax return, or needs to be on the Active Taxpayers List needs to be registered with FBR. Banks, government departments, large companies and tender authorities often ask for an NTN before they will do business with you. In Islamabad and Rawalpindi, landlords, shopkeepers, freelancers, consultants and contractors are among the most frequent applicants.
- Salaried individuals who want to file returns
- Sole proprietors, shopkeepers and traders
- Freelancers and IT service providers
- Partnerships and associations of persons (AOPs)
- Landlords with rental income
- Contractors bidding for government or corporate work

### How does NTN registration work for an individual?

An individual registers on IRIS using their CNIC, a mobile number registered in their own name, and an email address. FBR sends verification codes to the phone and email, and after verification the person's CNIC becomes their NTN. A business individual also adds business details such as the business name, address and activity.
The most common problems are SIMs not registered in the applicant's name, mismatched information, and incorrect business activity codes. Getting these right at registration avoids trouble with returns and sales tax later.

### How does a partnership or AOP get an NTN?

A partnership or association of persons is registered as a separate taxpayer. The principal officer applies on IRIS with the partnership deed, details and CNICs of all partners, and proof of the business address. FBR may also ask for a bank account certificate. Once approved, the firm receives its own NTN, which is used for its returns and bank account.

### What documents are needed for NTN registration?

Requirements depend on the type of taxpayer.
- CNIC of the individual, or of all partners for a firm
- Mobile number and email address in the applicant's name
- Business name, address and principal activity
- Proof of business premises, such as a rent agreement or ownership document
- Utility bill of the business premises
- Partnership deed for a firm or AOP

### Is an NTN the same as sales tax registration?

No. An NTN registers you for income tax. Sales tax registration (STRN) is a separate process for businesses that supply taxable goods or services above the thresholds set by law. Goods are registered with FBR; services in Islamabad are registered with FBR, and services in Rawalpindi with the Punjab Revenue Authority. Many businesses need both.

### What happens after you get an NTN?

An NTN does not by itself put you on the Active Taxpayers List. You must file your income tax return and wealth statement for the relevant tax year. Businesses may also need to file withholding statements if they deduct tax from payments to employees or suppliers. We can set up a simple yearly calendar so you do not miss deadlines.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps

We register individuals, sole proprietors and firms on IRIS, fix registration errors, and link your NTN to filing your first return. Send us your details by WhatsApp from anywhere in Islamabad, Rawalpindi or abroad, and we will confirm the documents and the fee before starting.

Q: Is my CNIC number my NTN?
A: For individuals registered on IRIS, yes: the CNIC number serves as the NTN.

Q: How long does NTN registration take?
A: Individual registration is often completed the same day once verification codes are received. Business and company NTNs can take longer if documents are requested.

Q: Do freelancers need an NTN?
A: Freelancers receiving foreign remittances benefit from registering and filing returns, and may qualify for reduced tax treatment on IT export income.

## Sales tax registration in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/sales-tax-registration/

Sales tax on goods is registered with the FBR under the Sales Tax Act 1990. Sales tax on services depends on where you provide them: in Islamabad it falls under the Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001, collected by the FBR; in Rawalpindi it is registered with the Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA). We register you and file monthly returns.

Process:
1. Assess your business: We confirm whether you deal in goods, services or both, and where.
2. Collect documents: We gather business, bank and premises details.
3. Register: We file with the FBR or PRA, including any biometric verification step.
4. Monthly filing: We file your monthly returns so you stay compliant.

Documents required:
- NTN and CNIC of owner or directors
- Business premises proof (rent agreement or ownership)
- Business bank account certificate
- Utility bill of business premises
- Photos and GPS location of premises, if required
- Electricity meter details for manufacturers

Laws: Sales Tax Act 1990; Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001; Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012

Key facts:
- Sales tax on goods is registered with the Federal Board of Revenue under the Sales Tax Act 1990.
- Sales tax on services provided from Islamabad is administered by FBR under the Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001.
- Sales tax on services provided from Rawalpindi is administered by the Punjab Revenue Authority under the Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012.
- Registration typically requires biometric verification and may involve verification of business premises.
- Registered persons must file monthly sales tax returns, even when there is no taxable activity in a month.

### Who needs sales tax registration?

You need sales tax registration if you manufacture, import, supply or deal in taxable goods above the thresholds set by law, or provide taxable services. Many businesses also register because large customers, government departments and tenders require an STRN from their suppliers. Retailers in certain categories must register and integrate their point of sale systems with FBR.
- Manufacturers and importers
- Wholesalers, distributors and certain retailers
- Service providers such as consultants, IT firms, contractors and advertisers
- Businesses supplying to government departments or large companies
- Restaurants, salons and other service businesses in the taxable categories

### FBR, ICT or PRA: where should you register?

This is where many businesses in the twin cities go wrong. Sales tax on goods is a federal tax collected by FBR wherever you are located. Sales tax on services is different: it depends on where the service is provided from. A service business operating from Islamabad registers for services tax with FBR under the Islamabad Capital Territory services law, while a service business operating from Rawalpindi registers with the Punjab Revenue Authority.
Some businesses supply both goods and services, or operate in both cities, and need more than one registration. We review your business model and tell you exactly which registrations apply.

### How does FBR sales tax registration work?

The applicant must first be registered for income tax on IRIS. The sales tax registration application is then filed on IRIS with business details, bank account information and details of the premises. The applicant, or the directors of a company, complete biometric verification at a designated facility. FBR may verify the business premises before activating the registration. Once approved, the business receives its sales tax registration and becomes liable to file monthly returns.

### How does Punjab Revenue Authority registration work?

For services provided from Rawalpindi, registration is done online on PRA's portal. The applicant provides business details, CNICs, bank information and proof of premises. After registration, the business files monthly returns with PRA and charges the applicable services tax on its invoices.

### What documents are needed for sales tax registration?

Keep these ready before applying.
- NTN and IRIS login details
- CNICs of the owner, partners or directors
- Business bank account certificate
- Proof of business premises: ownership document or rent agreement
- Utility bill of the premises
- Photographs of the premises and signboard where required
- Company incorporation documents or partnership deed

### What are your obligations after registration?

After registration you must issue proper sales tax invoices, keep records, and file monthly returns by the due date, even for months with no sales. Late or missing returns attract penalties and can lead to suspension of registration, which blocks input tax claims and may affect your customers. A monthly filing service keeps you compliant.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps

We determine whether you need FBR, ICT services or PRA registration, prepare and file the applications, guide you through biometric verification, and can file your monthly returns afterwards. The fee is agreed upfront.

Q: Do I register with FBR or PRA?
A: For goods, the FBR. For services, it depends on where the service is provided: Islamabad services fall under ICT (administered by FBR), Punjab services under the PRA.

Q: Do I have to file a return if I had no sales?
A: Yes. Registered persons generally must file a monthly return even when it is a nil return.

Q: What happens if I do not register?
A: Unregistered businesses that are required to register can face penalties, higher withholding and loss of business with clients who need sales tax invoices.

## Trademark registration in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/trademark-registration/

A trademark is registered with the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan (IPO Pakistan) under the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001. The process is: search, file an application in the right class, respond to examination, publication in the Trade Marks Journal for opposition, then registration. Registration lasts ten years and can be renewed.

Process:
1. Search: We check the register for similar marks.
2. File: We file your application in the right class.
3. Examination: We respond to any objections from the registrar.
4. Publication: Your mark is published for opposition.
5. Registration: You receive the registration certificate.

Documents required:
- Brand name and logo (if any)
- Applicant CNIC, or company incorporation certificate
- Description of goods or services
- Date of first use, if already in use
- Authorisation letter

Laws: Trade Marks Ordinance 2001; Trade Marks Rules 2004

Key facts:
- Trademarks in Pakistan are registered with the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan (IPO-Pakistan) under the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001.
- Goods and services are classified into international classes, and a separate filing is needed for each class.
- After examination, an accepted mark is advertised in the Trade Marks Journal, and third parties can oppose it within the time allowed by law.
- A registered trademark is valid for ten years and can be renewed for further ten-year periods.
- A search before filing reduces the risk of objection or opposition.

### Why should you register your trademark?

Your brand name and logo are business assets. Registration gives you the exclusive right to use the mark for the registered goods or services in Pakistan and a stronger legal basis to stop others from copying it. Without registration you may still have rights through use, but proving and enforcing them is harder, slower and more expensive. Registration also helps with online marketplaces, franchising, investment and selling the business later.

### What can be registered as a trademark?

A trademark is any sign that distinguishes your goods or services from those of others. It must be distinctive and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing mark in the same class.
- Brand names and business names used as brands
- Logos and stylised words
- Slogans and taglines, if distinctive
- Combinations of words, colours and devices
- Service marks for service businesses

### What is the trademark registration process in Pakistan?

The process at IPO-Pakistan has several stages, and it is normal for it to take many months from filing to registration.
- Search: check existing marks in the relevant class
- Filing: submit the application with the mark, class and specification of goods or services
- Examination: the registry examines distinctiveness and conflicts and may raise objections
- Reply to objections, if any, in writing or at a hearing
- Acceptance and advertisement in the Trade Marks Journal
- Opposition period for third parties
- Registration certificate issued if there is no successful opposition

### How do you choose the right class?

Pakistan follows the international classification of goods and services. A clothing brand files in the class for clothing; a restaurant files in the class for food and drink services; a software company may need classes for software and for IT services. Filing in the wrong class gives no protection where you need it, while filing in too many classes adds cost. Your lawyer will match your business to the right classes.

### What documents are needed?

Trademark filing needs only a few documents.
- Applicant's name and address (individual, firm or company)
- CNIC of the individual or authorised signatory
- Company incorporation certificate or partnership deed, if applicable
- The mark: word, or a clear image of the logo
- Description of goods or services and date of first use, if already in use
- Authorisation in favour of the lawyer or agent

### What happens if someone copies your trademark?

If your mark is registered, you can send a legal notice, oppose a conflicting application, and file a suit for infringement seeking an injunction and damages. If it is not yet registered, you may still have remedies for passing off based on prior use. Act quickly when you notice copying, and keep evidence such as invoices, advertisements and online listings that show your earlier use.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps

We search the register, advise on classes, file the application with IPO-Pakistan, respond to objections, and track your mark to registration. We also file oppositions and send infringement notices for businesses in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and across Pakistan. The fee is agreed before filing.

Q: How long is a trademark valid in Pakistan?
A: Ten years from the filing date, renewable for further ten-year periods.

Q: Can I use TM before registration?
A: Yes, TM can be used to claim a mark. The registered symbol should only be used once the mark is registered.

Q: How long does trademark registration take?
A: It usually takes many months because of examination and the opposition period. You get a filing number immediately, which establishes your priority date.

## Legal notice drafted by an advocate
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/legal-notice/

A legal notice is a formal letter from your advocate telling the other side what they owe you or must stop doing, and what legal action follows if they do not comply. It is often the fastest way to settle money recovery, rent, employment and contract disputes without going to court. Notices to government bodies are required before suing under section 80 CPC.

Process:
1. Tell us the facts: Share what happened and any documents.
2. We draft: Your advocate drafts the notice and you approve it.
3. We send: It is sent with proof of delivery.
4. Follow up: We advise on the reply or next legal step.

Documents required:
- Your CNIC
- Name and address of the other party
- Agreements, cheques, receipts, messages or emails
- Amount owed or action demanded

Laws: Code of Civil Procedure 1908, section 80 (notices to government); Defamation Ordinance 2002; Contract Act 1872

Key facts:
- A legal notice is a formal written demand sent by a lawyer before starting court proceedings.
- A suit against the government or a public officer generally needs prior notice under section 80 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908.
- A claim for defamation under the Defamation Ordinance 2002 requires a notice to the defendant before filing.
- Notices are usually sent by registered post or courier with acknowledgement, and copies are kept as evidence.
- A reply to a legal notice should be sent within the time it gives, usually after taking legal advice.

### What is a legal notice and when should you send one?

A legal notice tells the other party, in formal terms, what you claim, why you are entitled to it, and what you will do if they do not comply within a stated time. It is often the most cost-effective step in a dispute: many matters settle after a well-drafted notice because the other side sees that you are serious and have legal advice.
In some cases a notice is legally required before a suit can be filed, for example against the government under section 80 CPC, or for defamation under the Defamation Ordinance 2002. In other cases it is not mandatory but is good practice and helps show the court that you tried to resolve the matter first.

### What situations call for a legal notice?

We draft notices for individuals and businesses in Islamabad and Rawalpindi in situations such as these.
- Recovery of money, unpaid invoices or loans
- Dishonoured cheques
- Breach of a rent, sale or service agreement
- Eviction of a tenant or recovery of unpaid rent
- Defamation or false allegations
- Employment disputes, unpaid salary or wrongful termination
- Consumer complaints against sellers or service providers
- Harassment or misuse of personal information

### What should a legal notice contain?

A notice must be precise. Vague threats are easy to ignore; a clear claim with facts and dates is not. Your lawyer will include the key elements below and keep the tone firm and professional.
- Names and addresses of the sender and recipient
- A clear summary of the facts with dates
- The legal basis of the claim
- The specific demand: payment, action or stopping an activity
- A deadline for compliance
- The consequences of non-compliance, such as a suit or complaint

### How is a legal notice sent?

The notice is printed on the lawyer's letterhead, signed, and sent by registered post with acknowledgement due, courier with tracking, or both. Where appropriate, a copy can also be sent by email or WhatsApp. Proof of dispatch and delivery is kept, because the court may later ask whether the notice was served.

### What should you do if you receive a legal notice?

Do not ignore it, and do not reply in anger. Read the deadline, collect your documents, and speak to a lawyer. A careful reply can deny incorrect claims, put your own version on record and sometimes open the door to settlement. What you write in a reply may be used later in court, so it should be drafted with care.

### What happens if the other party does not respond?

If the deadline passes without compliance, you can proceed with the action stated in the notice, such as a civil suit for recovery, a summary suit on a negotiable instrument, a complaint, or a criminal case where the facts support it. Your lawyer will advise which forum in Islamabad or Rawalpindi is appropriate and what evidence is needed.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps

Send us the facts and documents by WhatsApp or the form on this page. A lawyer drafts the notice, reviews it with you, and dispatches it with proof of delivery. If you have received a notice, we draft a reply. Fees are agreed before work starts.

Q: Is a legal notice compulsory before filing a case?
A: Not always. It is required before suing the government (section 80 CPC) and before a defamation suit, and it is strongly advisable in most money and contract disputes.

Q: What if the other side ignores the notice?
A: You can proceed with a civil suit, recovery suit or other action. The notice becomes evidence that you tried to settle.

Q: How should I reply to a legal notice I received?
A: Do not ignore it. Have a lawyer reply within the time given, denying wrong claims, so the record reflects your position.

## Agreement and contract drafting
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/agreements/

A well-drafted agreement prevents most disputes. In Pakistan, agreements such as property sale and rent agreements are executed on stamp paper of the correct value, signed before witnesses, and in some cases registered with the sub-registrar. Our lawyers draft and review agreements so your money and rights are protected.

Process:
1. Tell us the deal: Parties, amounts, dates and conditions.
2. Draft: We draft the agreement in clear language.
3. Revise: You and the other party review changes.
4. Execute: We guide signing, witnesses, stamp paper and registration.

Documents required:
- CNIC copies of all parties
- Property documents, for property agreements
- Agreed terms (price, rent, duration, payment schedule)
- Two witnesses with CNICs

Laws: Contract Act 1872; Stamp Act 1899; Registration Act 1908; Partnership Act 1932

Key facts:
- Contracts in Pakistan are governed mainly by the Contract Act 1872.
- Most agreements must be written on stamp paper of the correct value under the Stamp Act 1899; e-stamp paper is used in Islamabad and Punjab.
- Rent agreements in Islamabad fall under the Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance 2001; in Rawalpindi, under the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009.
- Some documents, such as certain leases and sale deeds, must be registered with the Sub-Registrar under the Registration Act 1908.
- A clear dispute-resolution clause can save months of litigation if something goes wrong.

### Why should a lawyer draft your agreement instead of a template?

Templates copied from the internet are written for other countries or other deals. They often miss Pakistani requirements such as the correct stamp duty, registration, the right court or arbitration forum, and the specific obligations of your arrangement. When a dispute arises, the court reads what is written, not what the parties intended. A lawyer-drafted agreement records your actual deal clearly enough that a judge, or the other party, cannot misread it.
A good agreement also prevents disputes in the first place. When payment dates, deliverables, penalties and termination rights are spelled out, both sides know what to expect.

### Which agreements do people in Islamabad and Rawalpindi most often need?

We draft and review agreements for individuals, landlords, tenants, families and businesses. The most common are listed below.
- Rent and lease agreements for houses, flats, shops and offices
- Agreement to sell (bayana) for property
- Partnership deeds and shareholder agreements
- Service, supply and vendor contracts
- Employment contracts and non-disclosure agreements
- Family settlement deeds and gift (hiba) documentation
- Loan agreements and acknowledgments of debt

### What should every agreement include?

Whatever the type of agreement, certain clauses do most of the work when a problem arises. Your lawyer will tailor these to your deal.
- Full names, CNIC numbers and addresses of the parties
- A precise description of the property, goods or services
- Price, payment schedule and method of payment
- Duration, renewal and termination rights
- What happens on breach, including penalties or forfeiture of advance
- Dispute resolution: courts, mediation or arbitration, and the city
- Signatures of parties and two witnesses, with their CNICs

### What are the special rules for rent agreements in the twin cities?

Tenancy law differs between the two cities. In Islamabad, rent matters are governed by the Islamabad Rent Restriction Ordinance 2001 and disputes go to the Rent Controller. In Rawalpindi, the Punjab Rented Premises Act 2009 applies; it requires the tenancy agreement to be in writing and contemplates registration with the Rent Registrar, and disputes go to the Rent Tribunal.
In both cities, landlords are also expected to give tenant details to the local police under the applicable tenant-registration rules. Missing this step can cause problems for the landlord, so your lawyer will remind you to complete it.

### Does an agreement need to be on stamp paper or registered?

Most agreements need stamp duty paid under the Stamp Act 1899, usually through e-stamp paper. The amount depends on the type and value of the document. An unstamped or under-stamped document can still be admitted in evidence in some cases, but only after paying the duty and a penalty, so it is better to stamp it correctly at the start.
Registration is a separate question. Sale deeds, gifts of immovable property and leases above certain terms need registration with the Sub-Registrar. An agreement to sell is usually not registered, but a well-drafted one protects the buyer if the seller backs out.

### How long does it take to prepare an agreement?

A standard rent or service agreement can usually be drafted within one to two working days once we have the details. Complex shareholder or supply agreements take longer because they need discussion between the parties. Reviewing an agreement someone else has drafted is usually quicker, and we will mark the risky clauses and suggest changes.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps

Send us the details of your deal by WhatsApp or the form on this page. A lawyer drafts or reviews the agreement, explains each clause in plain language, and advises on stamp duty and registration in Islamabad or Rawalpindi. The fee is agreed before work starts.

Q: Does a rent agreement need to be registered?
A: Leases for more than one year must be registered under the Registration Act 1908. Shorter agreements are commonly made on stamp paper, and some areas also require tenant registration with police.

Q: Is an agreement on plain paper valid?
A: It can be valid as a contract, but insufficient stamp duty can make it inadmissible as evidence until the duty and penalty are paid.

Q: Can you review an agreement before I sign?
A: Yes. We review it and point out risky clauses before you sign.

## Court marriage in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/court-marriage/

Court marriage in Pakistan is a nikah performed with the free consent of both adults, usually at a lawyer's office, with a nikah registrar and two witnesses. The nikahnama is registered with the Union Council under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, after which a NADRA computerised marriage certificate can be issued. Both parties must be adults.

Process:
1. Consultation: We confirm eligibility and documents.
2. Affidavits: Both parties sign affidavits of free consent.
3. Nikah: The nikah is performed with witnesses.
4. Registration: We register the nikahnama and arrange the NADRA certificate.

Documents required:
- Original CNICs of bride and groom
- Passport-size photographs
- CNICs of two adult male witnesses
- Divorce or death certificate, if previously married
- Written permission of the arbitration council, if the man has an existing wife

Laws: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961; Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929 (and ICT Child Marriage Restraint Act 2025)

Key facts:
- In Pakistan, a court marriage is a nikah performed with the consent of both adults and registered under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961.
- Both parties must be of legal marriageable age; in Islamabad, the minimum age is 18 for both under the ICT Child Marriage Restraint Act 2025.
- The nikah is registered by a licensed Nikah Registrar and then with the Union Council, after which NADRA can issue a marriage registration certificate.
- A free-will statement or affidavit of the bride and groom is commonly prepared to record consent.
- Two adult Muslim witnesses are needed for the nikah.

### What does court marriage mean in Pakistan?

The phrase court marriage is commonly used, but the marriage itself is not performed by a judge. It is a nikah conducted with the free consent of both adults, usually arranged through a lawyer who prepares the documents, arranges a licensed Nikah Registrar and witnesses, and makes sure the marriage is properly registered. Lawyers often prepare affidavits of free will so that consent is clearly documented.
Couples choose this route when they want a simple ceremony, when families are not involved, or when they want to be sure the paperwork is correct from the start.

### Who can have a court marriage in Islamabad or Rawalpindi?

Any two Muslim adults who are legally eligible to marry each other can have a nikah. Both must consent freely. Legal age requirements apply: in Islamabad, the minimum age for marriage is 18 for both parties under the ICT law enacted in 2025. In Rawalpindi, Punjab law applies, and your lawyer will confirm the current requirement. Marriages involving a non-Muslim party, or a second marriage by a husband, have additional legal requirements.

### What is the court marriage procedure step by step?

The process is straightforward when documents are ready. It can often be completed in a single day, with registration following.
- Consultation and document check by the lawyer
- Preparation of affidavits or free-will statements of both parties
- Nikah performed by a licensed Nikah Registrar with two adult Muslim witnesses
- Completion and signing of the nikah nama, including the haq mehr and delegated rights
- Registration of the nikah with the Union Council
- Application for the NADRA marriage registration certificate

### What documents are needed for court marriage?

Keep originals and copies ready on the day.
- Original CNICs of the bride and groom
- CNICs of two adult Muslim witnesses
- Passport-size photographs of both parties
- Divorce or death certificate if either party was previously married
- Permission of the Arbitration Council if the husband has an existing wife
- Passport for foreign nationals or overseas Pakistanis

### Why do the nikah nama clauses matter?

The nikah nama is a legal document, and some of its columns affect your rights for years. The amount and form of haq mehr, whether it is prompt or deferred, and whether the wife is given the right of talaq (delegated divorce) are all recorded on it. Many couples sign without reading these columns. Your lawyer will explain each one so that both parties make informed choices.

### Is a court marriage legally valid and safe?

Yes. A nikah performed with free consent of adult parties and registered with the Union Council is legally valid. Registration is important: it provides official proof of the marriage for NADRA records, passports, visas and inheritance. If either party faces threats from family because of the marriage, a lawyer can advise on protection, including applications to the court.

### How MeraLawyer.pk helps with court marriage

We arrange the lawyer, Nikah Registrar and documentation in Islamabad or Rawalpindi, explain the nikah nama clearly, and complete registration with the Union Council so you can obtain the NADRA certificate. The fee is agreed before the day, and everything is handled discreetly.

Q: Can court marriage be done on the same day?
A: The nikah and affidavits can usually be completed the same day. Union Council registration and the NADRA certificate follow afterwards.

Q: Is court marriage legal without parents' consent?
A: Under Pakistani law an adult Muslim woman can marry with her own free consent. The nikah must still be properly registered.

Q: What is the minimum age for marriage?
A: Both parties must be adults. In Islamabad the minimum age for both is 18 under recent federal legislation, and you should confirm the current rule for the province where the nikah is registered.

## Khula in Pakistan: procedure and documents
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/khula/

Khula is a divorce initiated by the wife through the Family Court.
